title: Matching an import to a typed line or an expected item, the vary margin, the source ranking, est within 10%, and the possible double typed on two devices
written_in: SCHEMA_V3 6.4 and 12; DECISIONS_ROUND2 A6, F4, H2, H9, L (matching q1 to q13), M1, M2, O1, Q1, Q2, Q6, S1, S2
notes: Every amount is made up and in whole minor units (yen, so 1 is 1).
Dates: Fri 20 Nov 2026, Sat 21, Sun 22, Mon 23, Tue 24, Wed 25, Thu 26; Thu 10 Dec 2026, Fri 11, Sat 12, Mon 14.

An import line's day is its `posted` date when it has one, else its `date` (6.4). A typed line matches an import line inside its posting window either side of its day: from that day less the account's `postingDays` working days to that day plus them, both ends counted [F4; L matching q3]. On a card, the import line's buy date (`date`) or its posted date may fall in the window, and a card with no `postingDays` of its own has 7 working days [L matching q4, M1]. An expected item is settled by an import landing from 5 working days before its landing day to the end of its posting window after it [L matching q2].
`dir` is `out` (money leaving the account) or `in`. Expected items are named by schedule and unshifted due date, `pay@2026-12-12` [H2]; `lands` is the day after any weekend or holiday move.

Question `import`: the lines after every import is applied, as `gone` (line id to the id that removed it) and `settled` (occurrence name to the live line that settles it). Question `import_counts`: how many lines are gone and how many import lines are live. Question `import_dropped`: the import lines dropped as repeats of an equal-rank line [L matching q9]. Question `possible_doubles`: the pairs of typed lines offered as a possible double; nothing is removed. Question `not_double_mark`: what the answer "both are real" writes [L matching q12].

A statement import carries its own dates, `from` and `to` [L matching q8]; a screenshot read after it that falls inside those dates and matches no statement line is removed too, goneBy the statement import [M2]. An import may carry the `file` it was read from, and each of its lines the `line` it was on; with the type they are the line's `src`. A line's id for repeats is its date, amount, direction and count (the first, second, ... line with that date, amount and direction in its own import) [L matching q9].

Question `import_told` [O1]: each live imported line's `told`. An import that replaces a typed line keeps that line's `told`; one that replaces nothing keeps its own. Whether an unmatched import dated on a check's day or the setup day is inside that figure, and the printed running balance (`src.bal`) deciding the order, are in the reference model (scenarios/import_after_check.json).

Question `import_sides` [Q1]: an import line that meets one side of a two-sided record (a `transfer`, `repay`, `borrow` or `convert`, written with `k`, `acct`, the side the money leaves, and `acct2`, the side it reaches, and `a2` when what arrived differs [Q2]) attaches to it: it sets that side's posted date and source (`posted` and `src` for the side it leaves, `posted2` and `src2` for the side it reaches) and never replaces the record. A money-out line on `acct` meets the leaving side by `a`; a money-in line on `acct2` meets the reaching side by `a2` (else `a`), inside the posting window either side of the record's date. [S1] On a rough record (`est`) a side is met by a line within 10% of that side's amount and takes the line's amount; the other side keeps its typed amount, and in one currency the difference is a fee on the sender [Q2, S5]. The answer gives `attached` (record id to the sides set, each source as `{ type, file, line }`, and the record's `a` and `a2` when a side took a line's amount), `gone` as in `import`, and `live`, the import lines that became records of their own.

[Q6] Across one import, the line nearest an expected item's landing day settles it, then the line nearest its amount, then the first listed; items are taken in landing order. A later import with a nearer line moves the settle to it, whether read in the same check-in stretch (the same `grp`) [Q6] or a later one [S2]; so does a later import when the settle is held by an imported line already there (in `lines`, with its `settles`). [S2] A settle the person ticked at a check-in stays: the line carries `ticked: true` (the check-in's `settled` names it). A settle a typed line holds (a ticked `set:` record) stays as before. Dates added: Mon 7 Dec 2026.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A typed spend and its statement line, same day, same amount
cases.why: Same account, same direction, 1,200 = 1,200 exactly (t1 is not rough), posted Fri 20 is inside Fri 20 to Fri 20 + 1 working day. So t1 is replaced: gone, goneBy the import line i1 (6.4).

cases.question: import
cases.title: Posted on the Monday after a Friday buy, one working day window
cases.why: Window: Fri 20 plus 1 working day. Sat 21 and Sun 22 are not working days, so the window ends Mon 23. Posted Mon 23 is inside, so t1 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Posted one working day too late: both lines stay
cases.why: The window is Thu 19 to Mon 23 (Fri 20 less and plus 1 working day) [L matching q3]. Posted Tue 24 is after it, and on a bank account only the posted date counts, so nothing matches: t1 stays and i1 is a new line.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A Monday holiday stretches the window to Tuesday
cases.why: Mon 23 is a made-up holiday here, so Fri 20 + 1 working day skips Sat, Sun and Mon and lands on Tue 24. Posted Tue 24 is inside: t1 is replaced. Same lines as match-03, the holiday is the only change.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A card line posted six days after the buy, card window of 4 working days
cases.why: Fri 20 + 4 working days: Mon 23, Tue 24, Wed 25, Thu 26. Posted Thu 26 is inside, so t1 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: The same card line with the card default window: the buy date matches
cases.why: A card line matches by its buy date or its posted date, and a card with no window of its own has 7 [L matching q4]. The buy date, Fri 20, is the typed day itself, so it is inside the window and t1 is replaced. (The posted date, Thu 26, is 4 working days and 6 days after Fri 20, inside 7 either way.) Before L this was no match and the spend counted twice.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A different amount on a line that is not rough
cases.why: A typed spend that is not `est` matches only the exact amount [H9]. 1,180 is not 1,200, so both lines stay.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A rough line matches within 10%
cases.why: t1 is rough. 10% of 1,200 is 120; the difference is 1,200 - 1,180 = 20, which is not more than 120, so t1 is replaced [A6, H9].

cases.question: import
cases.title: A rough line at exactly 10% still matches
cases.why: 1,320 - 1,200 = 120, exactly 10% of 1,200. "Within 10%" includes the edge, so t1 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A rough line one yen past 10% of the typed amount still matches: 10% of the larger
cases.why: Within 10% means the difference is at most 10% of the larger amount, compared exactly in minor units [L matching q10]. The larger is 1,321; 1,321 - 1,200 = 121, and 121 x 10 = 1,210 is not more than 1,321, so t1 is replaced. Before L the margin was 10% of the typed 1,200 (120) and this did not match.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A refund of the same amount does not replace a spend
cases.why: 6.4 matches by direction: money in never matches money out, so the refund is a new line and the spend stays.

cases.question: import
cases.title: The same amount on another account does not match
cases.why: 6.4 matches by account first: a card line never replaces a typed bank line.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A power bill inside its vary margin settles its occurrence
cases.why: The margin is 30% of 8,000 = 2,400. 10,000 - 8,000 = 2,000, inside it; posted Wed 25 is inside Wed 25 + 1 working day. The import line settles power@2026-11-25 (6.4, last point).

cases.question: import
cases.title: A power bill past its vary margin settles nothing
cases.why: 10,500 - 8,000 = 2,500, more than the 2,400 margin. The occurrence stays unsettled (it will show as not seen yet after its window) and i1 is a new spend.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay at its exact amount settles its occurrence
cases.why: Same account, money in, 250,000 exactly, posted Thu 10 Dec on its landing day. The pay occurrence is settled by i1. (An exact amount matches whatever the margin is; with no `vary`, only the exact amount matches [L matching q1].)

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay moved before a weekend is matched on its landing day and named by its due date
cases.why: Due Sat 12 Dec, moved earlier to Fri 11. The window runs from the landing day, Fri 11, so the line posted Fri 11 matches. The occurrence keeps its name by the due date before the move, pay@2026-12-12 [H2].

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay posted one working day late still settles
cases.why: Thu 10 Dec + 1 working day = Fri 11. Posted Fri 11 is inside the window (H8 calls this pay late, expected), so it settles pay@2026-12-10.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay posted after its window does not settle it
cases.why: The window ends Fri 11 Dec. Posted Mon 14 is after it, so the import does not settle the occurrence automatically; it is a new line in. (The check-in list still lets the person tick it, A2.)

cases.question: import
cases.title: A statement replaces the screenshot lines it covers
cases.why: Statement ranks over screenshot (6.4). The statement covers Mon 16 to Sun 22 Nov, and a statement removes the screenshot lines inside its own dates, goneBy the statement import's id, f1 [L matching q8]. s1 (18 Nov) and s2 (19 Nov) are inside, so both are gone by f1; st1 and st2 are the live lines for that money. st3 matches nothing and is a new line. Before L each was goneBy its statement line (st1, st2).

cases.question: import
cases.title: A screenshot read after the statement loses to it
cases.why: The rank is statement over screenshot over typed, whichever arrives first. The screenshot line matches the statement line, so the screenshot line is the one that goes, goneBy st1. The 500 is counted once.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A screenshot replaces a typed line, then the statement replaces the screenshot
cases.why: First the screenshot: sc1 matches typed t1 and ranks over it, so t1 is gone by sc1. Then the statement (16 to 22 Nov): sc1 is a screenshot line inside its dates, so it is gone, goneBy the statement import f1 [L matching q8]. t1 stays gone (a gone line is never matched again). One live line, st1.

cases.question: import_counts
cases.title: Two coffees on the statement, one typed: one is replaced, one is new
cases.why: A replaced line is gone, and a gone line is never matched again, so the typed 500 can be replaced by only one of the two statement lines. The other is a second coffee nobody typed. Total spending 1,000, not 500 and not 1,500. (The import lines are applied in the order they are listed, so i1 is the one that takes the place of t1; the count does not depend on it.)

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: The same amount typed on two devices, same day, same place
cases.why: The device part of an id is its first part (section 0): aaaaaa and bbbbbb are two devices. Same day, same place (Free to spend), same 1,500: offered as a possible double [H9]. Nothing is removed; the person decides.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: Two lines from one device are not offered
cases.why: Both ids start with aaaaaa: one device, two page opens. H9 offers a double only for two devices (two lunches of the same price on one phone are normal).

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: Different day, different place or different amount: not offered
cases.why: Each pair differs in the day (20 and 21), the place (free and trip) or the amount (1,500 and 1,550). H9 needs all three the same.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: A gone line and an imported line are not offered
cases.why: The bbbbbb line was already removed, so there is nothing to ask about it. The cccccc line came from a statement, not typed on a device; an import is handled by the matching rule above, not by the double question.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A rough line and an import 10% of the larger apart: they match
cases.why: The larger is 1,333. 1,333 - 1,200 = 133; 133 x 10 = 1,330, not more than 1,333, so it is within 10% of the larger and t1 is replaced [L matching q10]. (10% of the typed 1,200 would be 120, and 133 is past it.)

cases.question: import
cases.title: One yen further: past 10% of the larger, no match
cases.why: 1,334 - 1,200 = 134; 134 x 10 = 1,340, more than 1,334 (the larger), so it is past 10% and nothing matches [L matching q10].

cases.question: import
cases.title: An import below the typed amount: the typed amount is the larger
cases.why: The larger is the typed 1,200. 1,200 - 1,080 = 120; 120 x 10 = 1,200, not more than 1,200: exactly at the edge, so it matches [L matching q10].

cases.question: import
cases.title: Half a minor unit is never rounded: a rough 1,205 and an import of 1,084
cases.why: The larger is 1,205; 10% of it is 120.5. 1,205 - 1,084 = 121; 121 x 10 = 1,210, more than 1,205, so no match. Compared exactly in minor units [L matching q10]: rounding the margin 120.5 up to 121 (as lookahead_ref.js did) would have matched.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A bill with no `vary`: one yen off settles nothing
cases.why: The power schedule has no `vary`, so only the exact 8,000 matches [L matching q1]. 8,001 is not 8,000: the occurrence stays unsettled and i1 is a new spend. At the check-in the person can tick the bill with the real amount (A2, F16).

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay landing 5 working days early settles its occurrence
cases.why: An import may settle an expected item up to 5 working days early [L matching q2]. Back from Thu 10 Dec: Wed 9, Tue 8, Mon 7, Fri 4, Thu 3 (Sat 5 and Sun 6 skipped). Posted Thu 3 Dec is the fifth working day before, so it settles pay@2026-12-10 (and F8 starts the period on 3 Dec).

cases.question: import
cases.title: Pay landing 6 working days early does not settle it
cases.why: The early limit is Thu 3 Dec (5 working days before Thu 10 Dec) [L matching q2]. Wed 2 Dec is before it, so the import is a new line in; the person can still tick the pay at the check-in (A2).

cases.question: import
cases.title: An import posted the working day before the typed date matches
cases.why: The window runs either side of the typed day [L matching q3]: Mon 23 less 1 working day is Fri 20 (Sat and Sun skipped), Mon 23 plus 1 is Tue 24. Posted Fri 20 is inside, so the person typed the wrong day and t1 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Two working days before the typed date: no match
cases.why: Tue 24 less 1 working day is Mon 23, so the window is Mon 23 to Wed 25 [L matching q3]. Posted Fri 20 is outside it; both lines stay.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A card line posted long after the buy matches by its buy date
cases.why: A card line matches by its buy date or its posted date [L matching q4]. Posted Wed 2 Dec is past the 7 day card window, but the buy date, Fri 20 Nov, is the typed day, so t1 is replaced and the spend counts once.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A card with a 1 working day window: the buy date is inside, the posted date is not
cases.why: The window is Thu 19 to Mon 23 (Fri 20 less and plus 1 working day). The posted date, Fri 27, is outside; the buy date, Mon 23, is inside, and on a card either one counts [L matching q4]. So t1 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: The same dates on a bank account: only the posted date counts
cases.why: L matching q4 gives the buy date to card lines only; a bank line is matched by its posted date (6.4). Posted Fri 27 is outside Thu 19 to Mon 23, so both lines stay.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A ticked pay replaced by its statement line: the settle moves to the import
cases.why: The pay was ticked at the check-in, so t1 settles pay@2026-12-10. The statement line matches t1 and replaces it, and the import takes over the typed line's `settles` [L matching q5], so the pay stays settled once, by i1, and is never counted twice.

cases.question: import
cases.title: An import that matches both a typed line and the expected item: the typed line wins and its settle moves
cases.why: Posted Mon 30 Nov is inside Fri 27 plus 1 working day, for both the typed line and the rent item. The typed line wins and is replaced by the import, which carries its settle [L matching q6]: t1 gone by i1, rent@2026-11-27 settled by i1. Rent counts once.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Two typed lines match one import: the closest date wins
cases.why: Both are inside the window (Wed 18 + 1 working day is Thu 19). t2 is dated Thu 19, 0 days from the import; t1 is 1 day away. The closest date wins [L matching q7], so t2 is replaced and t1 stays as a second coffee. Before L the earliest dated (t1) was taken.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Two typed lines the same distance away: the earliest `told` wins
cases.why: Posted Thu 19 is inside both windows (Wed 18 + 1 working day; Fri 20 - 1 working day) and 1 day from each. On equal distance the earliest `told` wins [L matching q7]: t2 was told at 08:00 on 20 Nov, t1 at 21:00 the same day, so t2 is replaced.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A misread screenshot line inside the statement's dates goes; one after them stays
cases.why: The statement covers 16 to 22 Nov. It removes the screenshot lines inside its own dates, matched or not, goneBy the statement import f1 [L matching q8]: s1 (matched by st1) and s2 (a misread 750 no statement line holds) are gone. s3, on 25 Nov, is after the statement's dates and stays.

cases.question: import_dropped
cases.title: Two screenshots overlapping: the repeated line is dropped, the new one kept
cases.why: b1 has the same line id as the live screenshot line a1: 18 Nov, 500, out, the first such line in its own screenshot. An equal-rank repeat with the same line id is dropped [L matching q9]. b2 (300 on 19 Nov) is new and kept.

cases.question: import_dropped
cases.title: The second of two coffees on a later screenshot is kept: the count is part of the line id
cases.why: shot2 shows two coffees of 500 on 18 Nov. b1 is the first such line (count 1), the same line id as a1, so it is dropped. b2 is the second (count 2); no live line has that id, so it is a coffee shot1 did not show and is kept [L matching q9].

cases.question: import_dropped
cases.title: One statement file read twice: every line with the same `src` is dropped, even one read differently
cases.why: f2 is the same file read again. j1 has the same src (statement, nov.pdf, line 1) and the same line id as i1, so it is dropped. j2 was read as 850, so its line id differs from i2's (800), but its src (nov.pdf, line 2) is the same, so it is dropped too [L matching q9]. The month is counted once.

cases.question: import_counts
cases.title: A repeat that is dropped is neither gone nor live
cases.why: j1 repeats i1 (same src, same line id) and is dropped, never added [L matching q9]. Only i1 is live: 1 live import line and nothing gone, so 1,200 is counted once.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: Two spends with the same budget line and no place: the line counts as the place
cases.why: Neither names a place; both name the budget line food. A budget line counts as the place [L matching q11], so two devices, the same day, the same place and 1,500: offered.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: "Both are real" is kept on the newer record: the pair is not offered again
cases.why: The pair is a possible double (double-01), but the person said both are real, which wrote `notDouble: [aaaaaa-x1y-3]` on the newer record [L matching q12]. So the pair is not offered again.

cases.question: not_double_mark
cases.title: What "both are real" writes
cases.why: The answer is kept as `notDouble: [id]` on the newer record [L matching q12]. bbbbbb-q2w-7 was told at 12:02, after aaaaaa-x1y-3 at 12:00, so it is the newer and gets notDouble naming the other.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: The same spend date typed on two different days is still offered
cases.why: "Same day" is the spend's date [L matching q13]: both are dated 20 Nov, though one was typed two days later. Same place, same 1,500, two devices: offered.

cases.question: possible_doubles
cases.title: The same day typed but different spend dates is not offered
cases.why: Both were typed on 20 Nov, but the spends are dated 19 and 20 Nov. "Same day" is the spend's date [L matching q13], so they are not offered.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A card line 6 working days (10 days) after the typed day: inside the card's 7 working days
cases.why: The card's default window is 7 working days [M1]. From Fri 20 Nov: Mon 23 (1), Tue 24 (2), Wed 25 (3), Thu 26 (4), Fri 27 (5), Mon 30 (6), Tue 1 Dec (7). The buy and posted date, Mon 30 Nov, is inside, so t1 is replaced. 7 calendar days would end on Fri 27 and the spend would count twice.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A card line 8 working days after the typed day: outside the card's 7 working days
cases.why: 7 working days from Fri 20 Nov end on Tue 1 Dec (match-44) [M1]. Wed 2 Dec is the 8th working day, and the line's buy date is the same day, so neither is inside: no match, and i1 is a new line beside t1.

cases.question: import
cases.title: A screenshot read after the statement: the unmatched line inside its dates goes too, goneBy the statement import
cases.why: The statement f1 (16 to 22 Nov) is read first, then the screenshot f2. sc1 matches st1 (500, 18 Nov), which ranks over it, so sc1 goes, goneBy st1, as in match-20. sc2 (750 on 19 Nov) matches no statement line but is inside the statement's dates, so it is removed too, goneBy the statement import f1 [M2]. sc3 (25 Nov) is after the statement's dates and stays a live line.

cases.question: import_told
cases.title: A statement line that replaces a typed line keeps the typed line's `told`
cases.why: Lunch typed at 12:00 on Wed 6 Jan and a check-in at 20:00 that held it. The statement line read on 13 Jan matches t1 and replaces it [A6]; it keeps t1's `told`, 12:00, so it stays inside the 20:00 check and is not counted again [O1]. Its own read time, 13 Jan 09:00, is not used.

cases.question: import_told
cases.title: A statement line that replaces nothing keeps its own `told`
cases.why: Nothing was typed, so the line replaces nothing and keeps its own `told`. Whether it is inside a check on its day is the model's rule: an unmatched import dated on a check's day or the setup day counts as inside that figure [O1] (scenarios/import_after_check.json iac-04, iac-06).

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: An ATM transfer typed as bank to cash, then the bank statement's plain line out: it attaches to the bank side
cases.why: The line is money out of the bank, 10,000, posted Mon 23 Nov: it meets the transfer's leaving side (bank, a 10,000, the same day). It sets that side's posted date and source and is not a record of its own, so the bank goes down by 10,000 once and the cash side's 10,000 stays [Q1]. Before Q1 the transfer was replaced by a one-sided line and the cash was lost (final_review_2 S1d).

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: An e-wallet top-up typed on Friday, the e-wallet statement's line in on Monday: it attaches to the reaching side as posted2 and src2
cases.why: Money in on the e-wallet, 1,000, posted Mon 23 Nov, inside Fri 20 + 1 working day: it meets the transfer's reaching side (the e-wallet). It sets `posted2` and `src2`, the second side's own posted date and source, so a current check of the e-wallet on Sat 21 does not hold the top-up [Q1, H1].

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: Both statements read: each side of the one transfer gets its own posted date and source
cases.why: The bank line out (Fri 20) meets the leaving side; the e-wallet line in (Mon 23) meets the reaching side. One record, two posted dates, two sources; nothing is added [Q1].

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A card payment ticked at the check-in, then the bank statement's line out: it attaches, the payment is never replaced
cases.why: Money out of the bank, 50,000, Thu 26 Nov: it meets the repay's leaving side. The repay stays, with its settle and its card side; the bank goes down by 50,000 once (final_review_2 S1b: before Q1, 200,000 where 250,000 was right) [Q1].

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A line in on the bank does not meet a transfer out of the bank: it is a record of its own
cases.why: A transfer out of an account matches that account's money-out line only [Q1]. 10,000 in on the bank (a refund, say) meets nothing and is a new line.

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A top-up with a fee: the bank line meets what left (a), the e-wallet line what arrived (a2)
cases.why: Pesos, in centavos. 1,015.00 left the bank and 1,000.00 arrived, so the record keeps `a2` [Q2]. The bank line out of 1,015.00 meets the leaving side by `a`; the e-wallet line in of 1,000.00 meets the reaching side by `a2` [Q1].

cases.question: import_dropped
cases.title: The same bank statement read twice: the second copy of an attached line is dropped
cases.why: The first read attaches i1 to the transfer's bank side, with source nov.csv line 4. The second read's line has the same source, an equal-rank repeat, so it is dropped [L matching q9], never a second 10,000 out.

cases.question: import
cases.title: Across one import, the line nearest the pay's day settles it, not the first in the file
cases.why: Both lines fit the pay: 30% of 250,000 is 75,000, and 50,000 and 12,000 are inside it; Mon 7 Dec is 3 working days early (up to 5 allowed). Thu 10 Dec is 0 days from the pay's landing day, Mon 7 Dec 3 days, so i2 settles it [Q6]. Before Q6 the first line listed (a returned deposit) settled it and the period started three days early (final_review_2 S8b).

cases.question: import
cases.title: Two lines as near as each other: the nearer amount settles
cases.why: Tue 24 and Thu 26 are each 1 day from Wed 25, both inside the window (5 working days before to 1 after), both inside 30% of 10,000 (3,000). 11,000 is 1,000 from 10,000 and 8,000 is 2,000 from it, so i2 settles [Q6].

cases.question: import
cases.title: A later import in the same check-in stretch with a nearer line moves the settle
cases.why: The first screenshot holds only Mon 7 Dec, so it settles the pay. The second, read in the same check-in stretch (`grp` k1, no check-in between), has Thu 10 Dec, 0 days from the pay against 3: the settle moves to it [Q6], and i1 is plain money in.

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A rough ATM transfer of 10,000, the bank's line 10,500: the bank side takes 10,500, the cash side keeps 10,000
cases.why: 10,500 - 10,000 = 500, and 500 x 10 = 5,000 is not more than 10,500, so the line is within 10% of the rough transfer's bank side and meets it [S1, Q1]. That side takes the line's amount, a = 10,500; the cash side keeps its typed 10,000 as a2; 10,500 - 10,000 = 500 is a fee on the bank [S1, Q2]. Before S1 the line was a record of its own (matching-open-1).

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A rough top-up of 1,000, the e-wallet's line 990: the e-wallet side takes 990, the bank side keeps 1,000
cases.why: 1,000 - 990 = 10, and 10 x 10 = 100 is not more than 1,000: within 10% of the reaching side, so the line meets it on Mon 23 Nov, inside Fri 20 + 1 working day [S1, Q1]. The e-wallet side takes 990 (a2); the bank side keeps its typed 1,000 (a); 1,000 - 990 = 10 is a fee on the bank [S1, Q2].

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A rough transfer of 10,000, the bank's line 11,500: more than 10% away, a record of its own
cases.why: 11,500 - 10,000 = 1,500, and 1,500 x 10 = 15,000 is more than 11,500: outside 10%, so the line does not meet the rough transfer and is a new line [S1, H9]. The transfer keeps 10,000 on both sides.

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A rough top-up met on both sides: the bank's 10,300 and the e-wallet's 10,000
cases.why: The bank line: 300 x 10 = 3,000, not more than 10,300, so the bank side takes 10,300 [S1]. The e-wallet side keeps its typed 10,000 (a2), and the e-wallet line of 10,000 meets it exactly [Q1]. 10,300 - 10,000 = 300 is a fee on the bank [S1, Q2].

cases.question: import_sides
cases.title: A transfer typed exactly (not rough), the bank's line 10,300: a record of its own
cases.why: S1 is about a rough side only. This transfer is not `est`, so a side is met only by its own amount, 10,000; 10,300 is a new line [Q1, S1].

cases.question: import
cases.title: A settle made by an import before a check-in moves to a nearer line read after it
cases.why: i1 (Mon 7 Dec, 3 days from the pay) settled the pay when it was read, in the stretch before a check-in (k1); nobody ticked that settle. i2, read in the next stretch (k2), is 0 days from the pay and inside 30% of 250,000 (12,000 off), so the settle moves to it, and the period start with it [S2, Q6]. Before S2 a settle of another stretch stayed (matching-open-2).

cases.question: import
cases.title: The same, but the person ticked that settle at the check-in: it stays
cases.why: The person ticked i1's settle at the check-in (`ticked`: the check-in's `settled` names it), so it stays although i2 is nearer (0 days against 3); i2 is plain money in [S2].

cases.question: import
cases.title: Two imports in two check-in stretches: the nearer line in the later one moves the settle
cases.why: The first screenshot (stretch k1) holds only Mon 7 Dec, 3 days from the pay, so it settles it. The second, read after a check-in (stretch k2), has Thu 10 Dec, 0 days from it: the settle moves [S2]; i1 is plain money in. Before S2 the settle of k1 stayed (matching-open-2; compare match-58, the same stretch).

open.question: A rough two-sided record in one currency where the line makes more arrive than left: a bank line out below the typed amount (an ATM withdrawal typed as 10,000, the bank shows 9,800), or an e-wallet line in above it. S1 says the side takes the line's amount and the difference is a fee on the sender (Q2), but a fee is what is lost when less arrives than leaves (the Q2 reading); here more arrived than left.
open.ref_does: The side takes the line's amount [S1], the other side keeps its typed amount, and nothing is a fee (a fee only when less arrived than left). So the receiving account shows more than left the sender. No case depends on it.
